# Contributing

The package separates search capabilities from agent-SDK adapters. Keep that
boundary intact: engine-specific request construction belongs in a tool module,
while framework imports and tool-object conversion belong in the adapter
module.

## Project structure

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/serpapi_search_tools/_shared.py` | Provider-neutral tool definitions, client runtime, schemas, and validation helpers |
| `src/serpapi_search_tools/_query_tools.py` | General web, news, maps, images, shopping, and video tools |
| `src/serpapi_search_tools/_travel_tools.py` | Hotels, flights, and travel-explore tools |
| `src/serpapi_search_tools/_providers.py` | Provider registry, aliases, dependency metadata, and auto-detection |
| `src/serpapi_search_tools/_adapters.py` | Lazy conversion into native SDK tools |
| `tests/` | Unit, schema, metadata, documentation, live, and integration tests |
| `examples/` | Direct and SDK-specific runnable examples |

## Add a search capability

1. Read the engine's official documentation from
   [SerpApi's LLM index](https://serpapi.com/llms.txt).
2. Define a public constructor with an explicit typed input shape. Required
   SerpApi inputs must be required model inputs.
3. Translate semantic values to native SerpApi parameters inside the callable.
4. Build a closed JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false`.
5. Add request-construction and validation unit tests, every-adapter schema
   tests, live coverage, docs, and an example.
6. Export the constructor from `serpapi_search_tools.__init__` and add it to the
   Great Docs API reference.

Do not add an arbitrary model-facing parameters dictionary. Developer-only
advanced filters belong in `default_params` until they deserve explicit typed
fields or a separate tool.

## Add an agent SDK

1. Add a `ProviderSpec` in `_providers.py` with one canonical provider name,
   intentional aliases, its distribution name, and optional-extra name.
2. Implement one lazy adapter in `_adapters.py` that consumes `ToolDefinition`.
3. Add the optional dependency range and an isolated tox factor.
4. Test missing-dependency behavior, native construction, exact schema
   preservation, and actual tool invocation against the fake OpenAI-compatible
   server when the SDK supports it.
5. Add a runnable example and an SDK documentation page.

The adapter must work for every public constructor. Do not special-case search
engines inside provider dispatch.

## Verification

Run the focused tests while editing, then follow the complete matrix in
[Testing](testing.html). Do not use live SerpApi or model calls in the default
unit suite.

## Test a release on TestPyPI

The **Publish main to TestPyPI** workflow is a manual release rehearsal. It
always checks out `main`, then runs source quality checks, builds the
distributions, smoke-tests and live-tests the exact wheel, and verifies all 14
supported SDK adapters before publishing.

Configure a protected GitHub environment named `testpypi`, restrict it to
`main`, and create a TestPyPI Trusted Publisher for workflow `testpypi.yml` and
environment `testpypi`. The live wheel gate also requires a repository secret
named `SERPAPI_API_KEY` or `SERPAPI_KEY`. No TestPyPI password or API token is
stored in GitHub.

Run the workflow from the Actions page with `main` selected. Duplicate versions
fail intentionally because TestPyPI does not allow a project version to be
uploaded twice. Bump `project.version` before another rehearsal.

## Publish documentation

Documentation builds and deploys only when a GitHub Release is published. The
release-triggered workflow renders Great Docs, repairs and verifies internal
links, and deploys the verified artifact to GitHub Pages. During ordinary pull
requests and branch development, use the local documentation commands in
[Testing](testing.html).
